sections.markdown:
## C — Getting your Nevada license, part two: young-driver penalties and requirements, instruction permits, passenger limits and curfew, license classes and restrictions, endorsements, renewals, address and name changes, ID cards, organ donation and fees
Knowledge domain: what a Nevada teen must do and avoid before and after licensing, how the instruction permit works, the limits on new teen drivers, what each license class and restriction code means, and the rules for renewals, record changes, ID cards, donor status and fees.

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
An applicant under 18 for a license, DAC or instruction permit needs a parent or guardian to co-sign and must sign an affidavit acknowledging the penalties that apply to young drivers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
A young driver's license can be revoked for 185 days when a blood, breath or urine test shows an alcohol level of at least 0.02% but less than 0.08% by weight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
Any court finding that a young driver drove under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance also brings a 185-day revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
Graffiti or defacing property, crimes tied to alcohol or a controlled substance, any use, possession, sale or distribution of a controlled substance, or buying, drinking or possessing alcohol can each mean suspension or delayed issuance for up to two years. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
Handling or possessing a firearm in violation of NRS 202.300 means suspension or delayed issuance for up to one year, and two years for a second offense. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
A first habitual-truancy offense brings a suspension of 30 days to 6 months or a 30-day delay; a second or later offense brings 60 days to 1 year or a 60-day delay (NRS 392.148). [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
A conviction for joining or organizing an unauthorized speed contest, or for driving in or facilitating an unauthorized trick driving display, brings a suspension of six months to two years. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
A young driver who becomes a first-time DUI offender faces the same penalties as a driver over 21. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
A teen applying for a license or DAC must present a driver's education Certificate of Completion and the Beginning Driver Experience Log (DMV Form DLD-130), filled in with blue or black ink before arriving for the drive test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
Anyone under 18 applying for an instruction permit must give the DMV a DMV-301 Certification of Attendance signed by the principal or a designated school official confirming minimum attendance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A01
A minor who has finished school submits the DMV-301 with a copy of a high school diploma or an equivalency (GED, HiSET or TASC), and the form must be signed and dated within the previous 60 days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A02
Driver's education can be completed at a local DMV-approved school or online through a DMV-approved school. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
Only a teen living more than 30 miles from an approved school who cannot take an online class may instead log 100 hours of behind-the-wheel driving, 10 of them in the dark. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
Teens within 30 miles of an approved driver's education school must complete 50 hours of supervised driving, 10 of them at night, recorded on the official DMV form. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
A minor must go six months without an at-fault crash, a moving violation conviction or any alcohol or drug conviction before receiving a license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A03
A Nevada instruction permit is valid for one year and must be carried whenever the holder drives. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A03
To get a permit you must be at least 15½, complete an application, pass a vision test and a knowledge test on traffic laws, signs, markings and safe driving, and have a parent or guardian available to authorize it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A03
A Class C permit holder may drive only with a licensed driver who is 21 or older, has at least one year of licensed experience and sits in the seat beside the permit holder. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A03
Applicants under 18 must hold an instruction permit for at least 6 months before applying for a license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A03
For their first 6 months of driving, new licensees who were 16 or 17 at issuance may not carry passengers under 18 except immediate family members (NRS 483.2523). [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A03
A minor may not drive between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. unless driving to or from a scheduled event, and this curfew lasts until the driver turns 18 regardless of when the license was issued. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A04
Every license class requires vision and knowledge tests, and a road test in the type of vehicle to be driven may also be required. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A04
A Class C holder who also wants to ride a motorcycle must pass a written test on motorcycle laws and practices and a motorcycle drive test. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A04
Any Nevada driver license class lets you ride a moped, or you can apply for a Class M license restricted to mopeds only. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A04
Class C covers cars, vans and pickups and may tow a vehicle of 10,000 pounds or less, and any combination of vehicles may not exceed 70 feet. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A04
Common restriction codes are B for glasses or contacts, F for added rearview mirrors, G for daylight driving only, 6 for a yearly vision exam, 7 for a yearly medical letter, 8 for a yearly driving test and JN for instruction permit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A05
An endorsement allows driving a vehicle that needs more skill than a typical vehicle, and each one needs additional tests. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A05
The J endorsement lets a Class C driver tow a vehicle or combination rated above 10,000 pounds, provided the combination stays within 70 feet and 26,000 pounds; above 26,000 pounds a Class A license is required. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A07
The expiration date is printed on the front of the license, and renewing on or before it is the driver's responsibility even though a renewal notice is mailed. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A07
Renewal may call for vision, knowledge and on-road driving tests to re-evaluate the driver and decide on restrictions. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A07
Nevada does not automatically extend licenses for military personnel, but active-duty members temporarily out of state may renew by mail. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A07
Nevada law requires you to report any change of address or name to the DMV within 30 days. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A07
Addresses can be changed online, at a DMV office or by mail with form DMV-22, but CDL holders must do it in person; name changes are always made in person with legal proof of the new name. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A07
Restricted licenses may go to drivers aged 14 and 15 who show family hardship or need to drive to and from school, and to people who have served half of a suspension or revocation. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A08
A Nevada ID card requires age 10 or older and lasts eight years, expiring on the birthday unless limited-term immigration documents were used. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A08
Being issued an ID card automatically surrenders your driving privilege and any ID card from Nevada or another state, whether or not you have it with you; seasonal resident ID applicants are the exception. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A08
Traffic citations issued to an ID card holder count against future driving privileges, and 12 or more demerits in 12 months means the privilege must be reinstated before a license can be issued. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A09
Organ Donor can be added to a license or ID card at original issuance, renewal or an address change, and a minor's parent or guardian signs an affidavit on the DMV-002 accepting that they cannot amend or revoke the donation. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A11
Fees are set by Nevada state law and can change; under age 65 an original license costs $41.25 and an instruction permit $22.25. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A11
Reinstatement after an alcohol or controlled-substance offense costs $120 plus a $35 victim's fee, while reinstatement for any other offense costs $75. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F41 | anchor: A12
Any suspension, revocation or cancellation requires paying the reinstatement fee, the original-license fee and any testing fees that apply. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0024]

Misconceptions: the teen curfew does not end when the passenger limit ends, it lasts until eighteen; a first-time DUI by a young driver is not treated more leniently than an adult's; getting an ID card is not neutral, it surrenders your driving privilege; Class C towing over ten thousand pounds needs the J endorsement, not a commercial license, until the combination passes twenty-six thousand pounds.
Mnemonics: fifteen and a half for the permit, six months holding it, six months with no young passengers; ten to five is curfew; fifty hours with ten at night, or one hundred with ten in the dark when far from a school.
Glossary: DLD-130 means the Beginning Driver Experience Log; DMV-301 means the school Certification of Attendance; endorsement means added permission for a vehicle needing more skill; restriction code means a letter or number on the license limiting how you may drive; reinstatement means restoring a suspended or revoked privilege.
Dynamic facts: fees are expressly subject to change, and forms, websites and phone numbers may be revised; confirm them on the Nevada DMV website.
